items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...relationships with trumpet players. Marvin Peterson, Naima, 1978... Then we’ll lead us to Freddie. But let’s talk about Marvin... [INTERVIEWEE] He moved back to . . .

ctx.x: That band, we were together for a minute. Went to Europe and worked a lot around the country, when it was still possible to do that.

Footnote – we’re coming back to that. Then, relationships with trumpet players. Marvin Peterson, Naima, 1978, and then The Angels of Atlanta, 1981. Then we’ll lead us to Freddie. But let’s talk about Marvin, because Marvin, I guess because he was an expatriate, that he doesn’t really have – he fell out of the public’s eye and ear.
